Q: How to perform the "uncollapsing" of a one row data frame or array to multiple rows in R A:

I like the outer() approach, it's clean and code-golf friendly so long as the values in collapsed are meaningful. If that is not a safe assumption, one can use this as well:

n <- ncol(collapsed)
Map(f = function(x, i) replace(rep(x, n), 1:n < i, NA),
    collapsed, seq_along(collapsed)) |>
  list2DF()
#   v1 v2 v3 v4 v5
# 1  1 NA NA NA NA
# 2  1  2 NA NA NA
# 3  1  2  3 NA NA
# 4  1  2  3  4 NA
# 5  1  2  3  4  5

Q: Rails When should I use strong parameters? A:

The easiest way to understand when you should use strong parameters is to understand what a mass assignment vulnerability is. In Rails 3 you could do the following:

class CreateUsers < ActiveRecord::Migration[3.0]
  def change
    create_table :users do |t|
      t.string :email
      t.string :encrypted_password
      t.boolean :admin
      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end


class UserController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new(params[:user])
    if @user.save
      redirect_to @user
    else
      render :new
    end
  end 
end

Here we are just passing a "hash" (its actually an ActionController::Parameters instance) straight into the model. All a malicious user has to do here is request:

POST /users?users[admin]=1

And they have created an admin account. In 2012 Egor Homakov famously exploited one such loophole in Github to commit to the Rails repository.

Such an attack is trivial to perform with cURL or by using the web inspector to manipulate a form.

If we allowlist which attributes the user should be able to pass:

class UserController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new(
      params.require(:user)
            .permit(:email, :password, :password_confirmation)
    )
    if @user.save
      redirect_to @user
    else
      render :new
    end
  end 
end

Then this avoids the vulnerability - strong parameters is really just a simple DSL for slicing and dicing nested hash like structures. What changed in Rail 4 is that when you pass an instance of ActionController::Parameters to a model an exception is raised unless calling #permitted? on the parameters object returns true. This avoids a mass assignment vulnerability from occurring simply due to programmer laziness or ignorance.

It does not sanitize your inputs in any other way. For example it won't prevent SQL injection or remote code execution if you treat user input carelessly.

You don't need strong parameters if you're passing parameters one by one like in this very contrived example:

class UserController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new do |u|
      u.email = params[:user][:email]
      u.password = params[:user][:password]
      u.password_confirmation = params[:user][:password_confirmation]
    end
    if @user.save
      redirect_to @user
    else
      render :new
    end
  end 
end

Q: MS Word VBA: Saving File, runtime error 5152 A:

The correct code VBA;

Option Explicit

Sub Splitter()

Application.ScreenUpdating = False

Dim Program As String
Dim DocName As String
Dim Letters As Integer, Counter As Integer
Dim filename As String, extension As String, Fullname As String, Mask As String
Dim i As Integer
Dim IllegalChars As Variant

Letters = ActiveDocument.Sections.Count
Selection.HomeKey Unit:=wdStory
Counter = 1

Mask = "yyyy-mm-dd_hhnnss"

While Counter < Letters
    DocName = "Reports" & LTrim$(Str$(Counter))
    ActiveDocument.Sections.First.Range.Cut
    Documents.Add
    Selection.Paste
    ActiveDocument.Sections(2).PageSetup.SectionStart = wdSectionContinuous
    
    filename = ActiveDocument.Paragraphs(1).Range.Text
    
    filename = Replace(filename, Chr$(13), "")
    filename = Replace(filename, Chr$(10), "")
    filename = Replace(filename, Chr$(11), "")
    
    IllegalChars = Array("/", "\", ":", "*", "?", """", "<", ">", "|", "&")
    For i = LBound(IllegalChars) To UBound(IllegalChars)
        filename = Replace(filename, IllegalChars(i), "_")
    Next i
    
    filename = Trim(filename)
    extension = ".docx"
    
    DocName = "E:\assessment rubrics\" & filename & " - Academic Program Review - " & Format(Now(), Mask)
    Fullname = DocName & extension
    
    ActiveDocument.SaveAs2 FileName:=Fullname, FileFormat:=wdFormatDocumentDefault, AddToRecentFiles:=False
    ActiveWindow.Close
    
    Counter = Counter + 1
Wend

Application.ScreenUpdating = True

End Sub

Q: Git error: RPC failed; HTTP 502 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 502 Proxy Error A:

I had the same issue. I undid my last commit via git reset and then again committed the changes. It resolved the problem.

Q: Building with MSBuild 14.0/C# 6.0 in AppVeyor A:

In addition to what you tried above, you need to make sure you used the Visual Studio 2015 image.

Q: Exception sending context initialized event to listener instance of class org.springframework.web.context.ContextLoaderListener A:

The stacktrace shows that you are referencing a missing library:

Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.openid4java.consumer.ConsumerException

Either you do not have openid4java installed or you have an older version of openid4java that doesn't contain the needed class.

You should install the correct version of openid4java
